pr_title: Fix loop in progress config flow
pr_body:
## Proposed change
When a progress config flow exists out of multiple progress actions, the config flow starts flickering when the first progress action is finished until it advances to the next step.

The frontend websocket connection receives a message to refresh the config flow both on following pieces of code: 
```py
self.hass.async_create_task(
    self.hass.config_entries.flow.async_configure(flow_id=self.flow_id)
)
``` 
```py
return self.async_show_progress(
        step_id="progress",
        progress_action=progress_action,
)
```        

So when for example task 1 is completed, the frontend ask an update and gets it, along with a new websocket message to refresh the config flow. This goes into an infinite refresh flow until the config flow finishes. 

A websocket message should only be sent out if the flow really changes (progress_action or the description_placeholders for in case you want to show a percentage of completion)
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/c433b251fa125789a2b8a68e67014d0eeb7bf6e0/homeassistant/data_entry_flow.py#L326-L336

To replicate the bug, you can use a custom integration from https://github.com/silamon/test_comp

Additional note: It is a must to guard against tasks being done before advancing to other tasks, since a step of a config flow can be multiple times refreshed during a progress config flow. The example in the documentation has been updated to reflect that in https://github.com/home-assistant/developers.home-assistant/pull/1856

--- 

Can this be included in the next patch/hotfix release? Thank you!

issue_context.title: Data entry flow with several Show Progress steps only executes first step
issue_context.body:
### The problem


When setting up a Data entry flow showing progress with several steps, only the first step seems to be executed and displayed on front end.

This is using the example from the documentation available here:
https://developers.home-assistant.io/docs/data_entry_flow_index#show-progress--show-progress-done

The code used for replicating is as follow:

manifest.json
```json
{
  "domain": "test_comp",
  "name": "Test Component",
  "codeowners": ["@hcoohb"],
  "config_flow": true,
  "iot_class": "local_polling",
  "version": "1.0.0"
}
```

\_\_init__.py
```py
from homeassistant.config_entries import ConfigEntry
from homeassistant.const import Platform
from homeassistant.core import HomeAssistant

PLATFORMS = [Platform.SENSOR]


async def async_setup_entry(hass: HomeAssistant, entry: ConfigEntry) -> bool:
    """Set up yeelight_bt from a config entry."""
    await hass.config_entries.async_forward_entry_setups(entry, PLATFORMS)

    return True


async def async_unload_entry(hass: HomeAssistant, entry: ConfigEntry) -> bool:
    """Unload a config entry."""
    unload_ok = await hass.config_entries.async_unload_platforms(entry, PLATFORMS)
    return unload_ok
```

sensor.py
```py
from homeassistant.components.sensor import SensorEntity
from homeassistant.helpers.entity_platform import AddEntitiesCallback
from homeassistant.config_entries import ConfigEntry
from homeassistant.core import HomeAssistant


async def async_setup_entry(
    hass: HomeAssistant,
    config_entry: ConfigEntry,
    async_add_entities: AddEntitiesCallback,
) -> None:
    """Add sensors for passed config_entry in HA."""
    async_add_entities([Base()])


class Base(SensorEntity):
    def __init__(self):
        self._attr_name = "Base"
        self._attr_has_entity_name = True

    @property
    def unique_id(self) -> str:
        assert self.name
        return "ID_" + self.name

    @property
    def state(self):
        return "hello"

```

config_flow.py
```py
from __future__ import annotations

import logging
from typing import Any
import asyncio

from homeassistant.config_entries import ConfigFlow
from homeassistant.core import callback
from homeassistant.data_entry_flow import FlowResult

DOMAIN = "test_comp"


_LOGGER = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class TempCompConfigFlow(ConfigFlow, domain=DOMAIN):  # type: ignore
    VERSION = 1
    task_one = None
    task_two = None

    async def async_step_user(
        self, user_input: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    ) -> FlowResult:
        """Handle a flow initialized by the user."""
        _LOGGER.info("async_step_user: %s", user_input)

        if user_input is None:
            return self.async_show_form(step_id="user")
        return await self.async_step_progress()

    async def async_step_progress(
        self, user_input: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    ) -> FlowResult:
        """Displaying rogress for two tasks"""
        _LOGGER.info("async_step_progress")
        if not self.task_one or not self.task_two:
            if not self.task_one:
                task = asyncio.sleep(10)
                _LOGGER.info("scheduling task1")
                self.task_one = self.hass.async_create_task(self._async_do_task(task))
                progress_action = "task_one"
            else:
                task = asyncio.sleep(10)
                _LOGGER.info("scheduling task2")
                self.task_two = self.hass.async_create_task(self._async_do_task(task))
                progress_action = "task_two"
            _LOGGER.info("showing_progress: %s", progress_action)
            return self.async_show_progress(
                step_id="progress",
                progress_action=progress_action,
            )
        _LOGGER.info("async_step_progress - all tasks done")
        return self.async_show_progress_done(next_step_id="finish")

    async def _async_do_task(self, task):
        _LOGGER.info("task pre")
        await task  # A task that take some time to complete.
        _LOGGER.info("task done")
        # Ensure we go back to the flow
        self.hass.async_create_task(
            self.hass.config_entries.flow.async_configure(flow_id=self.flow_id)
        )

    async def async_step_finish(
        self, user_input: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    ) -> FlowResult:
        _LOGGER.info("async_step_finish")
        return self.async_create_entry(
            title="Test_Comp",
            data={},
        )

    @callback
    def async_remove(self):
        """Clean up resources or tasks associated with the flow."""
        _LOGGER.info("async_remove")
        if self.task_one:
            self.task_one.cancel()

        if self.task_two:
            self.task_two.cancel()
```

translations\en.json
```json
{
    "config": {
      "flow_title": "Test Comp - ProgressFlow",
      "step": {
        "user": {
          "title": "Pre-progress",
          "description": "Two tasks of 10s will be started one after the other"
        },
        "progress":{
          "title": "Progress step",
          "description":"Progress step description"
        }
      },
      "progress": {
        "task_one": "This is the text for task ONE.",
        "task_two": "This is the text for task TWO."
      }
    }
  }
```

Expected behaviour:
When adding a  new Test_comp entry, we should see:
the progress for task one displayed for 10s with the text "This is the text for task ONE." 
 followed by the progress for task two displayed for 10s with the text "This is the text for task TWO." 
Then the successful dialog

Actual behaviour:
When adding a  new Test_comp entry, we see:
the progress for task one displayed for 10s with the text "This is the text for task ONE." 
Then the successful dialog
Task Two text is never showed and the task is cancelled before finishing.

Resulting Log:
```
2023-07-03 16:29:29.923 INFO (MainThread) [custom_components.test_comp.config_flow] async_step_user: None
2023-07-03 16:29:31.501 INFO (MainThread) [custom_components.test_comp.config_flow] async_step_user: {}
2023-07-03 16:29:31.502 INFO (MainThread) [custom_components.test_comp.config_flow] async_step_progress
2023-07-03 16:29:31.502 INFO (MainThread) [custom_components.test_comp.config_flow] scheduling task1
2023-07-03 16:29:31.502 INFO (MainThread) [custom_components.test_comp.config_flow] showing_progress: task_one
2023-07-03 16:29:31.504 INFO (MainThread) [custom_components.test_comp.config_flow] task pre
2023-07-03 16:29:41.506 INFO (MainThread) [custom_components.test_comp.config_flow] task done
2023-07-03 16:29:41.506 INFO (MainThread) [custom_components.test_comp.config_flow] async_step_progress
2023-07-03 16:29:41.507 INFO (MainThread) [custom_components.test_comp.config_flow] scheduling task2
2023-07-03 16:29:41.507 INFO (MainThread) [custom_components.test_comp.config_flow] showing_progress: task_two
2023-07-03 16:29:41.508 INFO (MainThread) [custom_components.test_comp.config_flow] task pre
2023-07-03 16:29:41.576 INFO (MainThread) [custom_components.test_comp.config_flow] async_step_progress
2023-07-03 16:29:41.576 INFO (MainThread) [custom_components.test_comp.config_flow] async_step_progress - all tasks done
2023-07-03 16:29:41.670 INFO (MainThread) [custom_components.test_comp.config_flow] async_step_finish
2023-07-03 16:29:41.680 INFO (MainThread) [custom_components.test_comp.config_flow] async_remove
```

Looking at the log, it seems that we go back inside the "progress" step straight away after scheduling the task 2, hence finishing the flow and cancelling the task2.
So task 2 is never finished but also the text for the progress "task_two" never seem to be shown.

I believe this is a bug, or else it might be that the documentation needs to be changed as it is confusing to show we can have several "progress" steps but only the first one is being displayed on front end...

I was about to open up an issue for the same problem. I've been spending days to figure out what's going on here. 

What happens is the following: 
1) You start the flow and task 1 is being executed
2) After 10 seconds task 1 is done and the below code updates the config flow: 
```py
self.hass.async_create_task(
    self.hass.config_entries.flow.async_configure(flow_id=self.flow_id)
)
``` 
3) A websocket message is being pushed to the frontend to force a refresh
4) The frontend is notified that it should refresh the config flow and ask an update through the api
5) The flow advances and task 2 is being executed
6) A websocket message is being pushed to the frontend to force a refresh
7) The frontend is notified that it should refresh the config flow and ask an update through the api
8) The flow advances while task 2 is still executing and moves on to the finish step. 

The example in the docs should be expanded to check if the task is done and still return the old progress_action if not. 
That would save a lot of time. 

---

When you've done that, you will start to see the config flow flickering when task 2 is executing because it's going in an infinite loop until it finishes. The websocket receives a message to refresh both on following pieces of code: 
```py
self.hass.async_create_task(
    self.hass.config_entries.flow.async_configure(flow_id=self.flow_id)
)
``` 
```py
return self.async_show_progress(
        step_id="progress",
        progress_action=progress_action,
)
```        

So when the frontend receives a websocket message because task 1 is completed, it ask an update and gets it, along with a new websocket message to refresh the config flow. 

A message should only be sent out if the flow really changes (progress_action or the description_placeholders for in case you want to show a percentage of completion)
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/c433b251fa125789a2b8a68e67014d0eeb7bf6e0/homeassistant/data_entry_flow.py#L326-L336
